title: Chiyya bar Rav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman considers it very likely that he was born after Rabbi Chiyya’s death, and Rav named him after his uncle. His father Rav studied with him, as in [Berakhot 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.53b.26) and [Nazir 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.66b.1), where he said to him, “My son, seize [the cup] and bless”;[^4] in [Pesachim 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.70a.5), “Rav taught Chiyya his son”; there, [113a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.113a.4), Rav said to him, “Do not drink drugs,” etc.; and in Moed Katan 20a he said to him, “In her presence observe mourning.”[^5] Likewise he raised objections to Rav Assi, as in [Ketubot 48b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.48b.4), [Kiddushin 46a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.46a.2) and [Keritot 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.17b.8-9).[^6] He likewise sat before Shmuel, as in [Arakhin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.9), and Shmuel said to him, “Son of a lion” or “son of the learned, come and I will tell you a fine thing that Rav your father used to say,” as in [Berakhot 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12a.28), [Chagigah 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.14a.3) and [Avodah Zarah 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.31b.11).

In Hyman’s account, all the great students of Rav were his teachers, as in [Eruvin 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.47a.9), “Rav Chiyya bar Ashi taught Chiyya bar Rav before Rav”; in [Eruvin 98b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.98b.16) and the [Jerusalem Talmud there, 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.1.21), with the additional locator ה., “Rav Chinena bar Shelamya taught him before Rav”; in [Shabbat 66a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66a.8) and in Yoma 15b as cited by Hyman, “Rav Chanan bar Rava taught him before Rav”; in [Eruvin 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.2b.15) and [14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.14a.12), “Rav Yehudah taught him before Rav”; and in [Avodah Zarah 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.8.6), “Shimon bar Chiyya taught him.”[^7] With Rav Huna he was like a colleague, for both sat before Shmuel, as in [Arakhin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.9); their disputes are in [Shabbat 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.69b.4-5), [Bava Batra 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.4b.9) and [Avodah Zarah 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.49b.10); in [Chullin 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.14a.2), “Rav Huna said: Chiyya bar Rav expounded in Rav’s name.” Hyman explains that only because Rav Huna headed the academy in Sura do we find in [Bekhorot 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.22a.5) that he called Rav Huna “my teacher.” It likewise appears from [Bava Batra 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.39b.4) that Chiyya bar Rav sat with Rav Huna, for they said there: “Giddel bar Minyomi … found Rav Huna, Chiyya bar Rav and Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi”; and so it is in the [Jerusalem Talmud there, 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.3.3.8): “Giddul bar Minyamin had a case, and his judges were Chilkiyah bar Tuvi, Rav Huna and Chiyya bar Rav.”[^8] Hyman describes his halakhot as few, saying that he is mentioned only in [Berakhot 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.14b.8), and Rav Huna bar Chinena spoke in his name, as in [Berakhot 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a.19);[^9] Rabbah bar Avuha asked him, as in [Avodah Zarah 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.51a.7); and we likewise find Abaye in his name, as in [Shevuot 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.17b.12). In Sukkah we find that he disagrees with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, but Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi. Of his personal events we find in [Yevamot 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.63a.12-13): when he saw that his mother was distressing his father, always doing the opposite of his father’s wish — when Rav wanted lentils, she made peas — what did he do? He told his mother that his father wanted peas, and she made lentils as his father wished. His father, who did not know that it was his son’s cleverness, said to him that his mother’s heart had turned for the good. Then his son told him that it was by his cleverness. Rav said to him: “This is what people say: The one who comes from you teaches you sense. But you, do not do so,” so as not to train oneself to speak falsehood.[^10]

In [Gittin 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.18a.13): his ketubah was written by day and signed at night, and Rav was there. At the supplied locator בב״ק פ״טז־ג [it is related] that Rav said to him, “Build me a house in the Land of Israel.” He merited a son great in Torah named Shimi, who was dear to Rav his grandfather, as in [Kiddushin 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.12a.14).[^3]

notes.text: ממקראיו הפרטים is rendered personal events. The original supplied locator בב״ק פ״טז־ג remains literal. A saved public request for Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma16:3 returns the explicit error that the tractate ends at chapter10; this is not absence proof. ToratEmet BereshitRabbah16:3 contains Rav asking his son Chiyya to build him a house in the Land of Israel, resolving the episode’s location without silently replacing Hyman’s abbreviation. The earlier note’s unresolved-Midrash question is retained historically and resolved by this named digital comparison. Rav naming his son after his uncle remains Hyman’s conjecture; my teacher renders רבי as an address to Rav Huna, not a global Rabbi title change. The mother-story’s always assertion is preserved. The additional Yerushalmi Eruvin locator ה. remains literal, without an established folio-side conversion.

The consulted Yevamot 63a distinguishes Rav’s wife reversing his food requests, Chiyya reversing what he tells her, and Rav’s warning against learning false speech. The adjacent account headed Rabbi Chiyya and his wife is a separate episode. Hyman’s always formulation remains his wording. The birth-after-Chiyya and naming-after-an-uncle hypothesis, all-great-students teacher classification, few-halakhot statement and explanation of the address my teacher remain his account. The supplied house-building locator בב״ק פ״טז־ג is preserved alongside the earlier disclosed Bereshit Rabbah 16:3 comparison; an invalid Jerusalem Talmud chapter request is not absence evidence. The collective named reports and Shimi’s genealogy are not newly merged into authority records.

The linked Bereshit Rabbah passage gives the house-building request. Yevamot distinguishes the wife reversing Rav’s requests from Chiyya reversing what he tells her. Chullin explicitly names Shimi as Rav’s grandson. Heilprin gives parallel traditions about Chiyya before Rav and Shmuel. See also [Bereshit Rabbah 16:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.16.3), [Chullin 111b (Shimi, Rav’s grandson)](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.111b.14). See [Heilprin’s parallel discussion](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1230&lang=en).
The named introduction is at the end of [Nazir 66a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.66a.12). The instruction continues at [Nazir 66b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.66b.1).
The mourning instruction cited as 20a occurs at [Moed Katan 20b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.20b.11), where Rav and Rav Huna are both reported to have addressed their sons.

[Ketubot 48b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.48b.4), [Kiddushin 46a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.46a.2) and [Keritot 17b:8-9](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.17b.8-9) all name Rav Huna or, alternatively, Chiyya bar Rav as the one who challenges Rav Asi.

Rav’s objection to Rav Chinena’s teaching in [Eruvin 98b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.98b.16) continues at [Eruvin 99a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.99a.1). The parallel in [Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:1:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.1.21) likewise names Chananiah bar Shelemya but concerns the doorway rule that Rav Yehudah teaches in [Eruvin 2b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.2b.15). [Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 4:8:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.8.6) names Shimon bar Chiyya as the teacher. Its Hebrew and Guggenheimer’s translation differ over who comes out from the curtain.

The accounts agree on the three participants. [Bava Batra 39b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.39b.4) reports either the ruling in Rav’s name or Chiyya giving it himself, after a protest in the first year. In [Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 3:3:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.3.3.8), Chiyya cites his father and the wording is the first three years.
At [Berakhot 30a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a.19), Rav Huna bar Chinena cites Chiyya bar Rav. Chiyya bar Avin is the speaker who responds.

The Yoma passage is at [Yoma 19b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.19b.6), where Rav signals the pronunciation of Kevutal’s name while reciting the Shema. Hyman cites 15b. In the separate case at [Shabbat 66a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66a.8), Rav signals that the two positions should be reversed.
